//: Cases for `python tools/toolcheck.py`. Data, not code, exactly like
//1: deploy.json -- adding a case must not require touching the runner.
//5: why      the bug this case exists to stop coming back. Required.
//6: needs    'any' | 'menu' (client at the main menu) | 'raid' (in a raid)
//7: write    true if the batch needs liveInspectorWrite + 'allow write'
//8: batches  list of batches. SEPARATE batches on purpose: per-batch
//9: anchors ($comp, $f1) do NOT survive across batches, and one
//10: of the historical bugs was exactly that they seemed to.
//11: assert   regexes that MUST appear in the normalised answer
//12: refuse   regexes that MUST appear AND are declared to be a REFUSAL.
//13: Reported separately, because 'the tool correctly declined'
//14: is the behaviour half these bugs broke, and a case with no
//15: refuse entry cannot lock it in.
//16: deny     regexes that must NOT appear -- the WRONG answer's shape.
//17: A refuse case without a deny is weak: it proves the
//18: refusal was printed, not that no answer was also printed.
//20: Answers are NORMALISED before matching: every pointer becomes <PTR>,
//21: every count-of-nodes/ms becomes <N>. Assert on names, shapes, counts
//22: and the FORM of an answer. Never on an address -- they change per run
//23: and an address assertion fails for a reason that is not a regression.

cases.name: channel-alive
cases.why: If the channel is dead every other case 'passes' by matching nothing. This must run first and its failure aborts the suite.

cases.name: roots-shape
cases.why: `roots` is how everything is reached. Its answer shape (transform + GameObject + name, two distinct anchors) is the contract every other case depends on.

cases.name: roots-lists-menu-ui
cases.why: The live UI is in DontDestroyOnLoad, which SceneManager excludes. Before `roots`, `find` searched only $preloader's subtree and reported names 'NOT PRESENT' that were merely unreachable.

cases.name: find-stopped-early-is-not-absence
cases.why: A bounded search that ran out of budget must SAY SO. Reporting a name as absent when the search merely stopped is a confidently-wrong answer.

cases.name: find-exhaustive-says-so
cases.why: The other half of the same contract: a search that DID cover the tree must be distinguishable from one that did not, or 'not found' means nothing.

cases.name: component-null-is-an-answer
cases.why: A failed component lookup must be reported as an ANSWER, not swallowed. When it was swallowed, $comp kept the PREVIOUS batch's pointer.

cases.name: comp-anchor-not-stale
cases.why: THE bug: a failed `component` left $comp holding the previous lookup's pointer, so the next `click`/`dump` acted on the wrong object and printed a complete, entirely fictional field map.

cases.name: gameobject-into-transform-walker-refused
cases.why: Feeding a GameObject to a Transform walker used to read a plausible childCount and INVENT a hierarchy of wrong children without faulting. Silence would be better; a refusal is correct.

cases.name: label-on-transform-is-not-empty-text
cases.why: `label` on a Transform reported `text = ""`, which reads as 'the label is empty' and is not an answer. It must say there is no text component.

cases.name: click-refuses-a-non-button
cases.why: `click`/`invoke` imposed UnityEngine.UI.Button's layout on ANY pointer, calling UnityEvent::Invoke on a GameObject and escaping the guard.

cases.name: write-gate-holds-without-allow-write
cases.why: liveInspectorWrite alone must not be enough; the batch must also say `allow write`. A write that goes through without it means the gate is decorative.

cases.name: open-refusal-names-a-reason
cases.why: `open` rejected a CORRECT target because the prologue snapshot had recorded our own trampoline. A refusal is acceptable; a refusal with no stated reason is not, because it is indistinguishable from that bug.

cases.name: state-explains-every-null-anchor
cases.why: `state` exists to say WHY an anchor is null. An anchor listed as null with no reason sends you hunting for an object the host simply has not learned yet.

cases.name: state-does-not-claim-not-in-raid-from-a-slot
cases.why: fact #51: `state` reported `in-raid anchor slot=-1` while a human WAS in a raid. A slot number is the anchor's binding, not the raid state, and must never be printed as if it were the raid state.
